channel.title: Cairo Desk
channel.description: A private daily round-up of Egyptian domestic politics, generated by Claude from Egyptian news sites.
channel.itunes:author: Cairo Desk

item.title: Cairo Desk – Saturday 31 October 2026
item.description: Running order: Pro-government TV host and MP Mostafa Bakry opposes the end of Sisi's term in 2030 and calls for a new constitution; Dostor's "chaos plan" warning names Mada Masr; Wafd party elects its Higher Authority; MP says farmers are jailed over Awqaf land rents; Briefly: Sisi returns from Russia and Hungary, draft laws on adultery penalty, Wafd finances; And finally: the qualifications for president.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Friday 30 October 2026
item.description: Prime minister tells medical graduates the state no longer guarantees jobs and concedes pay gap, citing the fifteen thousand pound minimum wage plan; parliament's six general debate requests; Al-Dostor opinion on the Egypt Forum and the Brotherhood; unconfirmed draft laws on penalty reduction for husbands; healthcare insurance claims in Minya; briefly: hacked Giza billboard, Mostaqbal Watan and governors; and finally, a retired general on 1967. Al-Ahram, Mada Masr and Al-Masry Al-Youm were unreachable today.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Thursday 29 October 2026
item.description: The constitution, term limits and succession after Sisi's Egypt Forum remarks, and the Hilal and Badrawi debate; the cabinet's sixty-five presidential directives and pay promises; district heads' powers in the local administration law; the Mostaqbal Watan party's Fayoum tour; Briefly: Police Academy student workshop and the foreign minister on water rights; And finally: the Badrawi and Moussa talk show quarrel.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Wednesday 28 October 2026
item.description: Running order: The president and the constitution, with a pro-government reaction; Sisi tells ministers to pull together on budget-agency debt; 2.2 million families leave Takaful and Karama, and an MP asks how; informal workers and social insurance; Senate debates food prices, plus a call to abolish the agricultural land tax; Briefly: Minya and Qena MPs meet the local development minister, Qalyubia deputy governor, Saudi authorisation headline; And finally: what parliament actually does. Sources: Al-Dostor and Al-Shorouk. Al-Ahram, Al-Masry Al-Youm and Mada Masr could not be reached.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Tuesday 27 October 2026
item.description: Parliament authorises the president to back Saudi Arabia in a closed session, with analysis of the procedure and the unpublished vote count; Prime ministerial decree gives the National Wages Council binding powers; Committee backs changes to the martyrs and victims compensation law; Cash instead of in-kind subsidy headline; Briefly: African Development Bank wastewater loan, the Egypt Forum, a Brotherhood commentary; And finally: a chorus of similar statements from MPs. Sources: Al-Dostor, Al-Shorouk, AFP background; Al-Ahram, Al-Masry Al-Youm and Mada Masr could not be reached.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Monday 26 October 2026
item.description: Stock exchange halts trading after ten per cent fall and the Cabinet says it is not a crisis; no fuel price rises or power cuts for now, says the government; fifteen thousand pound public sector minimum wage target; Farid Zahran's four economic principles; Al-Ghad, a backbencher and the limits of permitted speech; briefly, party farm machinery, party finance rules, housing buyers and cash subsidies; and finally, poultry self-sufficiency.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Sunday 25 October 2026
item.description: The Egypt Forum closes, with cabinet saying its decisions bind the government from 2027; the forum's debt target and no-new-tax pledge, as reported by a Senate member in Al-Dostour; a rise in the wheat procurement price to 2,650 pounds an ardeb; a six-month window for coded electricity meters and simplified building-violation reconciliation; a parliamentarian calls the forum the second phase of the national dialogue; briefly: pro-government praise, a Brotherhood commentary, tourism financing; and finally, a talk-show host on the 'near-state'.

item.title: Cairo Desk – Saturday 24 October 2026
item.description: Running order: Egypt Forum closes as Sisi says recovery from 2011 will take decades; Parliament delays vote on helping defend Saudi Arabia; Government unveils economic transformation programme with growth targets; Central bank governor cites reserves and a five year convertibility goal; Briefly: assault cases, a viral police video, Brotherhood series; And finally: presidential directives for apartment buyers. Sources: Al-Dostor and Al-Shorouk; Al-Ahram, Al-Masry Al-Youm and Mada Masr could not be reached.
